claims.text: Systematic shifts in the d-band center govern catalytic activity, selectivity, and durability in transition-metal catalysts when morphology, nanoparticle size, and support interactions are held constant.
Controlled secondary-metal doping or alloying can systematically shift the catalyst d-band center without changing nanoparticle size or support interactions.
Fixed reaction conditions and physical catalyst properties make observed performance changes attributable solely to electronic-structure modifications.
The catalyst d-band electronic structure can be characterized using XPS or UPS and supported by computational estimates.
Doping modifies the intrinsic d-band center.
Changes in the d-band center alter the binding energies of key reaction intermediates.
An upward shift in the d-band center enhances adsorption of reaction intermediates.
Enhanced intermediate adsorption from an upward d-band-center shift can increase catalytic activity.
Changes in adsorption strength affect selectivity and durability through a trade-off between reaction kinetics and surface poisoning.
A moderately upshifted d-band center will yield greater catalytic activity than the undoped baseline.
A moderately upshifted d-band center will alter product selectivity relative to the undoped baseline.
A moderately upshifted d-band center will change durability, with the direction determined by the balance of adsorption strength.
The proposed relationship should hold only over a doping range in which morphology and nanoparticle size remain unchanged.
The d-band-center relationship may cease to apply when other structural parameters dominate performance.
A controlled series with incrementally shifted d-band centers and matched size, morphology, and support interactions can test the proposed causal relationship.
Failure to observe corresponding performance trends after confirming d-band shifts and constant structural factors would falsify the proposed governing role of the d-band center.

contradictions.description: The conditions field states that fixed conditions ensure performance changes are attributable solely to electronic structure, whereas the uncertainty field allows subtle structural variations and secondary effects beyond pure electronic effects to influence performance.
